subject: [hw] K02 -> IK: your 5 calls are wired; one call missing on your side (client close)
body:
Wired exactly as your contract, and the staged compile of sweet_touch.c (q10at3 + 0298 + your 0299 patch + the three .inc + the two headers) passes with the CI flags -Wall -Wextra -Werror; all 162 undefined symbols of the object exist in kernel.development.nord2-metal-q10at3.

1) struct n2vr_hw: my start initialises it with TWO static functions in nord2_vcodec.inc:
     struct n2vr_hw hw = { n2vc_relay_hw_ioctl, n2vc_info_fill };
     bool relay = n2vr_start(&hw);
   NOTE: hw.ioctl must be n2vc_relay_hw_ioctl, NOT n2vc_ioctl: n2vc_ioctl takes my per-open struct n2vc_open *, yours takes (dev_t,...,struct proc *). n2vc_relay_hw_ioctl finds/creates the per-(minor 1, proc) state and calls n2vc_ioctl; it is static in my file, so your snippet is replaced by mine (your snippet names it n2vc_ioctl, which would be a type error if copied).
2) minor 0 d_open -> n2vr_server_open(); d_close -> n2vr_server_close(): done.
3) d_ioctl first line: if (n2vr_relay_cmd(cmd)) return n2vr_ioctl(dev, cmd, data, flag, p): done (before I look up my open state).
4) DMA: my record keeps owner (struct n2vc_open *, which holds minor + struct proc * + flags); the check is literally n2vr_dma_allowed(owner->minor, owner->proc, flags, f->minor, f->proc) and returns EACCES when false. Free is owner-only. I switched my EPERM to EACCES so the integrated path is consistent.
5) MISSING ON YOUR SIDE: a clients DMA buffers must be freed at its last close (frozen header: "owned by the open file that allocated them (freed on close)"). Your hw struct has no close callback and n2vr_client_close does not tell me. Please add ONE line in n2vr_client_close, on the last-close path (where c->state becomes CLOSING or is freed), outside n2vr_lock:
     n2vc_relay_closed(p);      /* K02: free this clients DMA handles and power references */
   Declare it in your file as `void n2vc_relay_closed(struct proc *p);` (defined in mine, non-static; it finds the minor-1 state by proc and destroys it). Without it a client that exits without RWVC_DMA_FREE leaks its pool pages until a later open of the same proc reuses the state. My host test covers the free path through n2vc_open_destroy; the call itself is untested on the kernel side.
Also: redwood_vcodec.h is copied to bsd/dev by make_patch.sh, so my plain #include "redwood_vcodec.h" is fine (same as yours).
